item.title: Wisbech High Street redevelopment plans approved
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech High Street redevelopment plans approved
Fenland District Council has approved plans to redevelop a vacant site on Wisbech High Street. The project will see the construction of commercial premises and six one-bedroom flats at numbers 11 and 12, with access provided via Castle Mews. The site has remained empty since the original Grade II listed buildings were demolished in 2020.
During a meeting on Wednesday, September 23, councillors described the two-decade delay in bringing the site back into use as embarrassing. Council leader Chris Boden has called for an explanation regarding previous administrative issues that stalled the development. Local representatives have welcomed the decision, noting that the project is a positive step for the town.

item.title: King’s Lynn sleep out raises over £7,000 for local night shelter
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn sleep out raises over £7,000 for local night shelter
A charity sleep out in King’s Lynn has raised more than £7,000 to support the town’s night shelter. Around 30 people spent Friday night in the grounds of the Minster to experience the challenges of sleeping rough. The funds will help the shelter, which relies entirely on community support and grants, as it prepares to reopen its doors on October 8.
The shelter is now appealing for food donations, including tinned goods, breakfast items, and long-life milk, to stock its cupboards for the winter season. Anyone interested in volunteering or donating can find further information on the King’s Lynn Night Shelter website or by calling 01553 776109.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech academy hosts talks on the future of Fenland soil
The Green Skills Academy in Wisbech has hosted a collaborative session focused on the future of agriculture and peat soil in the Fens. The event brought together the Fenland Environmental Network and the non-profit group Fenland SOIL to discuss the long-term sustainability of the local landscape.
Organisers say the meeting provided a space for education providers and environmental groups to share expertise on land use and food production. The session aligns with the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Local Skills Improvement Plan, which highlights sustainable land management as a priority for the region. The College of West Anglia says the initiative aims to help students gain the skills needed to support the local economy’s shift toward a more sustainable future.

item.title: MP calls for Ely Junction upgrades to improve Fen Line services
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
MP calls for Ely Junction upgrades to improve Fen Line services
South West Norfolk MP Terry Jermy is urging the Transport Secretary to prioritise upgrades to Ely Junction. Following a summer that saw hundreds of cancellations on the Fen Line, Mr Jermy met with the Fen Line Users’ Association to discuss the impact on passengers in King’s Lynn, Downham Market, and Watlington.
The MP highlighted issues including poor service reliability, cleanliness, and faulty air conditioning. While acknowledging that extreme weather has affected local peat soils, he argued that many delays remain avoidable. Mr Jermy is now pushing for the project to be included in the next government Spending Review to boost regional growth. Meanwhile, a new scheme launched on September 20 now allows passengers to use alternative operators if their train is cancelled.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/call-for-improvements-as-rail-users-suffer-summer-of-misery-9484577/
